title: Over a henselian pair, idempotents lift uniquely in integral algebras
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], i.e. for every finite $A$-algebra $B$ every idempotent of $B/IB$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $B$. Let $A\to C$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings with $C$ integral over $A$ (every element of $C$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in the image of $A$), and let $IC$ be the ideal of $C$ generated by the image of $I$. Then the quotient map $C\to C/IC$ induces a bijection from the set of idempotents of $C$ to the set of idempotents of $C/IC$: every idempotent of $C/IC$ is the image of an idempotent of $C$, and two idempotents of $C$ with the same image in $C/IC$ are equal.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.11.6 (Tag 09XI, lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, line 2553), implication (3)$\Rightarrow$(4): (3) is the definition [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], (4) is this statement; Stacks proves it via (3)$\Rightarrow$(1)$\Rightarrow$(5)$\Rightarrow$(2)$\Rightarrow$(4)

proof.text: *Finite subalgebras.* Let $\varphi:A\to C$ be the structure map and $x_1,\dots,x_n\in C$ finitely many elements. Let $C'\subseteq C$ be the $A$-subalgebra generated by $x_1,\dots,x_n$, i.e. the subring generated by $\varphi(A)$ and the $x_j$, an $A$-algebra via $\varphi':A\to C'$ ($\varphi'(a)=\varphi(a)$), and let $j:C'\hookrightarrow C$ be the inclusion, an injective $A$-algebra map. (a) $C'$ is a finite $A$-algebra: each $x_j$ is integral over $A$ as an element of $C$, i.e. $p_j(x_j)=0$ in $C$ for a monic $p_j\in A[T]$ (coefficients acting through $\varphi$); since $C'$ is a subring of $C$ containing $x_j$ and $\varphi(A)$, the same equation $p_j(x_j)=0$ holds in $C'$, so $x_j$ is integral over $A$ as an element of $C'$. The $x_j$ generate $C'$ as an $A$-algebra, hence $C'$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators]. (b) $j(IC')\subseteq IC$: an element of $IC'$ is $\sum_k\varphi'(i_k)y_k$ with $i_k\in I$, $y_k\in C'$, and $j$ maps it to $\sum_k\varphi(i_k)y_k\in IC$. (c) If $z\in C'$ and $z=\sum_{k=1}^m\varphi(i_k)y_k$ in $C$ with $i_k\in I$ and every $y_k\in C'$, then $z\in IC'$: the right-hand side is computed inside the subring $C'$ (as $\varphi(i_k)=\varphi'(i_k)\in C'$), so it is the element $\sum_k\varphi'(i_k)y_k$ of $IC'$, and it equals $z$ because $j$ is injective. Note that $z\in IC$ alone does not give $z\in IC'$; this is why the witnesses $y_k$ are put into the generators of $C'$ in steps 2 and 3.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.11.6 (Tag 09XI, lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, line 2553), (3)$\Rightarrow$(4); agent-written reduction to finite subalgebras in place of the Stacks chain (3)$\Rightarrow$(1)$\Rightarrow$(5)$\Rightarrow$(2)$\Rightarrow$(4)

proof.text: *Existence.* Let $\bar e\in C/IC$ be an idempotent. Choose $c\in C$ mapping to $\bar e$ (the quotient map is surjective). Since $\bar e^2=\bar e$, $c^2-c\in IC$, so we may choose finitely many $i_1,\dots,i_m\in I$ and $y_1,\dots,y_m\in C$ with $c^2-c=\sum_{k=1}^m\varphi(i_k)y_k$ (the witnesses: any expression of $c^2-c$ as a finite $C$-linear combination of elements of $\varphi(I)$, which exists by definition of the ideal $IC$). Let $C'\subseteq C$ be the $A$-subalgebra generated by $c,y_1,\dots,y_m$. By step 1(a) $C'$ is a finite $A$-algebra, and by step 1(c), applied to $z=c^2-c\in C'$ with the $y_k\in C'$, $c^2-c\in IC'$, so the class $\bar c'$ of $c$ in $C'/IC'$ is an idempotent. As $(A,I)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], there is an idempotent $e'\in C'$ whose class in $C'/IC'$ is $\bar c'$, i.e. $e'-c\in IC'$. Put $e=j(e')\in C$. Then $e^2=j(e'^2)=j(e')=e$, and $e-c=j(e'-c)\in IC$ by step 1(b), so $e$ is an idempotent of $C$ mapping to the class of $c$, which is $\bar e$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.11.6 (Tag 09XI, lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, line 2553), (3)$\Rightarrow$(4); agent-written reduction to finite subalgebras in place of the Stacks chain (3)$\Rightarrow$(1)$\Rightarrow$(5)$\Rightarrow$(2)$\Rightarrow$(4)

proof.text: *Uniqueness.* Let $e,f\in C$ be idempotents with the same image in $C/IC$. Then $e-f\in IC$; choose $i_1,\dots,i_m\in I$ and $y_1,\dots,y_m\in C$ with $e-f=\sum_{k=1}^m\varphi(i_k)y_k$. Let $C'\subseteq C$ be the $A$-subalgebra generated by $e,f,y_1,\dots,y_m$; it is a finite $A$-algebra by step 1(a). In $C'$, $e$ and $f$ are idempotents (the equations $e^2=e$, $f^2=f$ hold in the subring), and $e-f\in IC'$ by step 1(c) applied to $z=e-f$. So $e$ and $f$ are two idempotents of $C'$ lifting the same idempotent of $C'/IC'$ (the class of $e$). By the uniqueness in the definition of a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], $e=f$ in $C'$, hence in $C$. Steps 2 and 3 together say that the map from idempotents of $C$ to idempotents of $C/IC$ (well defined, as a ring map sends idempotents to idempotents) is surjective and injective, i.e. a bijection.
